pack.name: Backup & Cleanup
pack.description: Protect data and reclaim disk: scheduled database backups, folder mirrors, temp-file sweeps, and log rotation.

templates.name: Daily Database Backup
templates.description: Back up a PostgreSQL database on a schedule with pg_dump.

parameters.label: Database user
parameters.help: The PostgreSQL role to connect as.

parameters.label: Database name
parameters.help: The database to back up.

parameters.label: Backup file path
parameters.help: Where to write the .sql dump.

templates.name: Weekly System Cleanup
templates.description: Delete temporary files on a schedule to reclaim disk space.

parameters.label: Path to clean
parameters.help: Files/glob to delete, e.g. %temp%\*.

templates.name: Backup Folder to Zip
templates.description: Compress a folder into a .zip archive on a schedule.

parameters.label: Folder to back up
parameters.help: Folder (or glob) to compress. Avoid single quotes in the path.

parameters.label: Destination .zip
parameters.help: Where to write the archive. -Force overwrites an existing file.

templates.name: Mirror Folder (robocopy)
templates.description: Mirror a directory to a backup location with robocopy /MIR.

parameters.label: Source folder
parameters.help: The directory to mirror from.

parameters.label: Destination folder
parameters.help: The backup directory. /MIR makes it match the source exactly (deletes extras).

templates.name: Backup a Registry Key
templates.description: Export a Windows Registry key to a .reg file on a schedule — a lightweight way to snapshot configuration before it drifts or before a risky change.

parameters.label: Registry key path
parameters.help: Full registry path to export, e.g. HKLM\SOFTWARE\MyApp.

parameters.label: Output .reg path
parameters.help: Where to write the exported key. /y overwrites an existing file.

templates.name: Back Up a SQLite Database
templates.description: Make a consistent copy of a SQLite database with its built-in backup command on a schedule, which is safe to run while an application is using the database, unlike copying the file directly.

parameters.label: Database file path
parameters.help: Absolute path to the SQLite database file to back up. The sqlite3 command-line tool must be installed and on the PATH.

parameters.label: Backup file path
parameters.help: Absolute path of the backup file to write. It is overwritten on every run, so point it at a dated name or rotate it separately if you want history. Avoid spaces in both paths.

templates.name: Back Up a Git Repository as a Bundle
templates.description: Write a complete, single-file copy of a git repository with all its branches and tags using git bundle on a schedule, so a lost laptop or a force-pushed remote does not take the only copy of your history with it.

parameters.label: Repository path
parameters.help: Absolute path to the local git repository.

parameters.label: Bundle file path
parameters.help: Absolute path of the .bundle file to write, ideally on a different drive or a synced folder. It is overwritten on every run, so rotate it separately if you want history.

templates.name: Back Up a Folder with restic
templates.description: Take an encrypted, deduplicated snapshot of a folder into a restic repository on a schedule, so you keep a browsable history of every run for the cost of only what changed, which a plain zip or mirror cannot give you.

parameters.label: Folder to back up
parameters.help: Absolute path to the folder whose contents are snapshotted. The restic command-line tool must be installed and on the PATH.

parameters.label: Repository path
parameters.help: Absolute path of an existing restic repository, created once beforehand with restic init. Put it on a different drive or a synced folder, not next to the source.

parameters.label: Password file path
parameters.help: Absolute path to a file containing only the repository password, readable by the account that runs the task. Losing the password means losing the backups.

templates.name: Back Up a MySQL / MariaDB Database
templates.description: Write a full logical dump of one MySQL or MariaDB database to a file on a schedule with mysqldump, for the database engine the catalog’s PostgreSQL and SQLite backups do not cover.

parameters.label: Database user
parameters.help: The MySQL account to connect as. Store its password in a client option file such as my.cnf under a client section, because this command never prompts and never puts a password on the command line.

parameters.label: Database name
parameters.help: The database to dump. The mysqldump tool must be installed and on the PATH.

parameters.label: Backup file path
parameters.help: Absolute path of the .sql file to write, with no spaces in it. It is overwritten on every run, so rotate it separately if you want history.

templates.name: Back Up a MongoDB Database
templates.description: Write a compressed archive of one MongoDB database to a file on a schedule with mongodump, for the document store the catalog’s PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite backups do not cover.

parameters.label: MongoDB connection URI
parameters.help: The connection string including the database name, with no spaces in it. A password in the URI is stored in the task, so prefer a local or credential-free connection. The mongodump tool must be installed and on the PATH.

parameters.label: Archive file path
parameters.help: Absolute path of the .gz archive to write, with no spaces in it. It is overwritten on every run, so rotate it separately if you want history.

templates.name: Redis Snapshot (BGSAVE)
templates.description: Ask a Redis server to write an RDB snapshot to its own disk in the background on a schedule with redis-cli. This triggers the snapshot on the server; it does not copy the file anywhere else.

parameters.label: Redis host
parameters.help: The hostname or address of the Redis server. The redis-cli tool must be installed and on the PATH.

parameters.label: Redis port
parameters.help: The port the Redis server listens on. This command sends no password, so the server must allow unauthenticated access from this machine.

templates.name: Purge the pip Download Cache
templates.description: Delete every wheel and HTTP response pip has cached on a schedule to reclaim disk space; the next install simply downloads again. This only touches pip’s cache, never installed packages.

templates.name: Create a System Restore Point
templates.description: Create a Windows system restore point on a schedule, so there is a rollback point from before the week’s driver and application changes. This snapshots system state, not your files — pair it with a file backup rather than replacing one.

parameters.label: Restore point description
parameters.help: The label shown in System Restore. Avoid single quotes (they close the PowerShell string).

templates.name: Delete Files Older Than N Days
templates.description: Prune files in a folder that are older than a cutoff, to reclaim disk.

parameters.label: Folder to prune
parameters.help: Directory whose old files are deleted (recursively).

parameters.label: Older than (days)
parameters.help: Delete files last modified more than this many days ago.

templates.name: Empty Recycle Bin
templates.description: Empty the Windows Recycle Bin on a schedule.

templates.name: Purge Old Items from the Trash (macOS)
templates.description: Permanently delete items that have sat in the macOS Trash longer than a number of days, on a schedule, so deleted files stop holding disk space without wiping something you binned this morning.

parameters.label: Older than (days)
parameters.help: Items last modified more than this many days ago are deleted permanently. The job may need Full Disk Access to read the Trash.

templates.name: Docker Cleanup (prune)
templates.description: Reclaim disk space by pruning unused Docker containers, networks, and images.

parameters.label: Extra prune flags
parameters.help: Optional extra flags, e.g. --volumes or -a (removes ALL unused images).

templates.name: Claude Code Log Cleanup
templates.description: Housekeeping companion for the scheduled Claude runs: delete run logs/digests older than a cutoff so they do not pile up. Read-nothing, deletes only matching files in one folder.

parameters.label: Log folder
parameters.help: Folder holding the Claude run logs to prune.

parameters.label: File filter
parameters.help: Which files to consider, e.g. claude-*.log or *.md.

parameters.label: Keep for (days)
parameters.help: Delete matching files older than this many days.

templates.name: Postgres Vacuum & Analyze
templates.description: Run VACUUM ANALYZE against a PostgreSQL database on a schedule to reclaim bloat and keep the query planner’s statistics current — routine maintenance, not a backup.

parameters.label: Database user
parameters.help: The PostgreSQL role to connect as.

parameters.label: Database name
parameters.help: The database to vacuum.
